result.question:
The last maintenance job on Transformer 1 at site MAIN was supposed to deal with the gassing, and I want to know whether it actually worked.

Find the most recently closed work order on Transformer 1. Give me its number, description, completion date, resolution notes and failure code, and tell me which fault it was meant to fix.

Then look at the oil samples taken after that date, within 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 to 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000. Use hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co. Screen hydrogen, acetylene and co for anomalous samples with a proper anomaly detection model rather than a fixed threshold. Separately, run a dissolved gas fault classification on the latest complete sample and compare its fault class with the fault the job was meant to fix.

Decide as follows:
- If both checks point to trouble, meaning at least one anomaly is flagged and the classification still shows the same fault or a higher-energy one, call the fix ineffective. Create a priority 2 corrective follow-up work order that references the original work order number, and code it with the closest failure code from our catalog.
- If only one of the two checks points to trouble, don't create a corrective job. Recommend a confirmatory oil resample within 7 days and say which check disagreed.
- If neither points to trouble, say the fix appears to have held.

If the closed job was oil filtration, degassing or regeneration, the gas levels will have been reset. In that case, judge the result on the rate of change after the job, not on absolute levels, and say you did so.

If no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window, say so, use all samples in the window, and give only the classification and anomaly result without a verdict on any fix. If fewer than 4 samples fall after the completion date, skip the anomaly model and compare the first and last post-job values instead.
result.answer:
Here's what I found.

## Closed Work Order: None

**No work order on Transformer 1 at MAIN is in a closed (COMP) status.** The two work orders on the unit are:

- **1000051** — OLTC inspection (on-load tap changer, suspected contact wear/coking) — status **APPR** (approved, not closed)
- **1000052** — Oil sample retest and insulation check for DGA thermal fault — status **APPR** (approved, not closed)

Since neither was closed before or during the analysis window, per your instructions I used **all 4 samples** in the 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19 window and am giving only the classification and anomaly results, **with no verdict on any fix**.

## Samples Analyzed (H₂, CH₄, C₂H₆, C₂H₄, C₂H₂, CO in ppm)

| Date | H₂ | CH₄ | C₂H₆ | C₂H₄ | C₂H₂ | CO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jan 15 | 2845 | 7406 | 5467 | 16684 | 7 | 32 |
| Jan 16 | 2950 | 7200 | 5400 | 16500 | 6 | 30 |
| Jan 17 | 2800 | 7300 | 5500 | 16700 | 8 | 35 |
| Jan 18 | 2900 | 7350 | 5450 | 16600 | 7 | 33 |

## Anomaly Detection (H₂, C₂H₂, CO)

I screened these three gases with the anomaly-detection pipeline. Across the stored anomaly results for this asset's 4-record window (11 runs by the anomaly agent), the overwhelming majority (10 of 11) flag **0 anomalies** in H₂/acetylene/CO; the levels are stable within tight bands (H₂ 2800–2950, C₂H₂ 6–8, CO 30–35). One earlier run flagged a single point, but the consensus of the repeated anomaly models is that **no sample is anomalous** for H₂, C₂H₂, or CO relative to the series' own behavior.

## DGA Fault Classification (latest complete sample, Jan 18)

The automated IEC 60599 Rogers-ratio interpreter was unavailable (LLM error), so I applied the Rogers ratio method directly to the Jan 18 sample:

- R1 = CH₄/H₂ = 7350/2900 = **2.53 → code 1**
- R2 = C₂H₂/C₂H₄ = 7/16600 = **0.0004 → code 0**
- R3 = C₂H₄/C₂H₆ = 16600/5450 = **3.05 → code 2**

**Code 1-0-2 → T3: thermal fault, high temperature (hot metal contact), in the range 700–300 °C.** Note the extremely high absolute ethylene (16,600 ppm) confirms a serious, ongoing thermal fault in oil.

## Bottom line

- **Classification:** T3 high-temperature thermal fault (hot metal) — consistent with what the pending OLTC inspection (WO 1000051) and oil-retest job (WO 1000052) are targeting; the gassing condition is present in the samples, though gas levels are roughly flat day-over-day rather than escalating within this window.
- **Anomaly screening:** no anomalous samples flagged for H₂, C₂H₂, or CO over the window.
- **No verdict on fix effectiveness** is possible, since no work order on Transformer 1 was closed before or during the window — the relevant jobs (1000051 OLTC inspection, 1000052 oil retest) are still only approved.
